answer: The mechanism is a capital cost that cannot be amortised across identities. Each identity must post its own stake before it earns anything, and the stake binds to one registered key, so a second identity needs a second fully-funded stake rather than a reuse of the first. Splitting one operator into a thousand wallets multiplies the locked capital by a thousand while payouts stay per-identity, turning a sybil farm into a negative-yield venture. The ocean of clones is expensive, the glacier of locked funds never melts, and a juniper earns nothing until its stake is real.
